articles.title: La emotiva carta de un aficionado del Tenerife a Jesús de Miguel: "Hay algo que nadie podrá arrebatarnos..."
articles.standfirst: Un hincha leyó una misiva dedicada al jugador en el minuto de silencio en el Heliodoro
articles.summary: Un hincha leyó una misiva dedicada al jugador en el minuto de silencio en el Heliodoro
articles.body: Un aficionado leyó una carta dedicada al jugador en el minuto de silencio en el Heliodoro y puso los pelos de punta a todos los asistentes a un homenaje en el que las emociones estaban a flor de piel. "Vino a luchar por el ascenso, lo conseguimos, pero se nos fue muy pronto. Hoy el corazón del tinerfeñismo está de luto. Cuesta encontrar palabras cuando alguien que ha formado parte de nuestra historia se marca demasiado pronto. Cuesta aceptar que ya no estás, que tu esfuerzo, tu pasión por este escudo, por todo lo que diste, se quedan para siempre en nuestros recuerdos. Llegaste hace poco a nuestra familia blanquiazul, pero el tiempo no entiende de huellas ni de sentimientos. En muy poco tiempo te ganaste un lugar en nuestros corazones y con tu trabajo, tu compromiso y tu aportación, te convertiste en una parte importante de una historia que siempre llevaremos con orgullo. Porque hay personas que, aunque estén poco tiempo, dejan una marca que perdura para siempre. Demi, lo tuyo no es una marca, lo tuyo ya es una leyenda. La temporada pasada fuiste mucho más que un jugador. Fuiste una pieza importante de un equipo que entre todos: afición, directiva, equipo, luchó y sufrió y soñó hasta conseguir el ansiado ascenso. Formaste parte de una historia que siempre llevaremos en el corazón. De esos momentos que nos hicieron sentir orgullosos de nuestros colores y que ahora, con tu ausencia, tristemente, adquieren un valor todavía más especial. Nos duele tu marcha, Demi. Nos duele pensar que ya no volveremos a verte defender esta camiseta, que no habrá más celebraciones, más abrazos ni más momentos compartidos. Pero hay algo que nadie podrá arrebatarnos. Todo lo que nos diste, todo lo que aportaste y la huella imborrable que has dejado como 9 en el Club Deportivo Tenerife y en su afición. Hoy el fútbol queda en un segundo plano. Hoy no importan los resultados ni objetivos. Hoy sólo importa recordar a la persona, al compañero, al futbolista, a su familia. Que ayudó a escribir una página bonita de nuestra historia. Gracias por formar parte de este camino, por defender nuestros colores y regalarnos motivos para sentirnos orgullosos. Ya formas parte de la historia blanquiazul. Te lo has ganado con orgullo, con fuerza, con corazón. Y una historia que no se mide únicamente en temporadas, partidos o goles, sino también en sentimientos, recuerdos y personas que jamás se olvidan. Y tú, Jesús, serás imborrable para todos los blanquiazules. Te marchas demasiado pronto, pero nunca te irás del todo. Tu nombre quedará ligado a aquel ascenso, aquellos goles, aquella ilusión compartida y una familia blanquiazul que hoy llora tu pérdida. El templo, nuestro templo tinerfeño, el Heliodoro y el Tinerfeñismo y los blanquiazules nunca te olvidarán. Descansa en paz".

articles.title: Philip Rivers, NC State Reportedly Have 'Momentum' in Contract Talks to Replace Dave Doeren as HC
articles.summary: The potential return of Philip Rivers to NC State, this time as the head coach of the program, grows more real by the day.
articles.body:
The potential return of Philip Rivers to NC State, this time as the head coach of the program, grows more real by the day.

According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports, "The two sides are expected to have further communication in the near future and there's continued momentum at the moment toward Rivers ultimately being the hire, sources tell CBS Sports. Nothing final at this point though."

Rivers, 44, played his college ball for the Wolfpack, throwing for 13,484 yards, 95 touchdowns and 34 interceptions across four seasons. He then went on to have a highly successful NFL career that included stops with the Los Angeles Chargers (2004-19) and Indianapolis Colts (2020; 2024) and may ultimately result in a Hall of Fame induction.

Hot Seat Check on Struggling NFL Coordinators 🌡️

Between his first and second stints with the Colts—and currently—he's served as the head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama, where he's led the program to the state semifinals over the past two seasons. He also interviewed with the Buffalo Bills about their previous head-coaching vacancy ahead of the 2026 campaign.

For NC State, Rivers would be a splashy, energizing hire for the program after Dave Doeren was fired on Oct. 24 following a 31-28 loss against Stanford and 3-4 start to the season. And while that move appears to be gaining steam, Rivers didn't offer much insight into the possibility over the weekend.

"N.C. State is special to me," he told Ben Thomas of AL.com on Friday night. "Coach Doeren, what he did over 14 years, all-time winningest coach, I have a ton of respect for what he did and how he went about it with the University. There is nothing there at this point. You understand the chatter that is out there. You take it one day at a time. I'm excited about this postseason with these guys. Like I said last year, you never say never, but there is nothing imminent."

articles.title: Así queda la clasificación de la Champions League: el PSG se afianza en el liderato y el Atlético se complica
articles.standfirst: Todos los detalles sobre los equipos de la máxima competición europea
articles.summary: Todos los detalles sobre los equipos de la máxima competición europea
articles.body: La presente edición de la Liga de Campeones recupera el pulso con la cuarta jornada de la fase de liga. Los principales clubes continentales buscan sumar más puntos para tomar posiciones tempranas de cara a la clasificación final. Este martes, tres equipos españoles disputaban su duelo, todos de local. El FC Barcelona, que tropezó ante el PSG, goleó al Aston Villa de Unai Emery por 3-0. El Villarreal, se enfrentaba al líder PSG en La Cerámica fue vapuleado por 0-6. Mientras el Atlético de Madrid disputaba uno de los partidos más destacados de la jornada ante el Bayern de Múnich, y terminó perdiendo 0-2 y se queda con solo cuatro puntos. Real Madrid y el Betis jugarán este miércoles a domicilio. Los blancos visitarán Atenas para medirse al AEK. Los béticos, visitarán el Signal Iduna Park del Borussia Dortmund. El PSG se coloca líder indiscutible con un pleno de victorias con 12 puntos y 20 goles a favor. Los de Flick, se ponen segundos con 9 unidades, habiendo tres equipos españoles (Betis y Real Madrid) dentro del Top 8. (*) Equipos con un partido menos. Los conjuntos favoritos saltan al terreno de juego sabiendo que sumar triunfos desde el inicio resulta vital para evitar cruces complicados y no tener que hacer cuentas en las últimas jornadas. Esta emocionante fecha inicial pondrá a prueba el nivel físico de las plantillas de élite, que buscan situarse rápidamente en la zona alta que otorga el billete directo. En este innovador sistema de competición, los ocho primeros clasificados al finalizar la liguilla obtienen el billete directo a los octavos de final. Por su parte, los clubes situados entre la novena y la vigesimocuarta posición disputarán una eliminatoria de repesca a doble partido para completar la fase eliminatoria. Finalmente, los equipos que terminen entre el puesto veinticinco y el treinta y seis quedarán eliminados de forma definitiva de la competición.

articles.title: SEC Coach Shuts Down FSU Speculation amid Latest Rumors on HC Vacancy After Mike Norvell Firing
articles.summary: After firing head coach Mike Norvell on Sunday, Florida State will have to look elsewhere if it was planning on targeting Missouri's Eli Drinkwitz.
articles.body:
After firing head coach Mike Norvell on Sunday, Florida State will have to look elsewhere if it was planning on targeting Missouri's Eli Drinkwitz.

During his press conference on Tuesday, Drinkwitz used his opening statement to put an end to any speculation that he could replace Norvell.

"I'm not a candidate at Florida State," Drinkwitz told reporters. "I want to clear that up. Let's focus on the main thing, which is Texas, and let's eliminate all the distractions and clear the clutter from that standpoint for my team and for everybody out there."

On3.com's Pete Nakos listed Drinkwitz among the "names to know" in the Seminoles' head coaching search.

In his seventh season at the helm of the Tigers, Drinkwitz has led the team to a 6-2 start and a No. 19 ranking in the AP Top 25 ahead of Saturday's home matchup against No. 10 Texas.

While Drinkwitz would surely be a strong candidate to take over at Florida State, he sounds content to stick with Missouri going forward.

articles.title: Birmingham 3-0 Millwall: Alex Cochrane, Max Bird and Jay Stansfield net in Blues win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Birmingham City and Millwall at St Andrew's on Tuesday night; Alex Cochrane, Max Bird and Jay Stansfield net in Blues victory.
articles.body:
Cochrane, Max Bird and Jay Stansfield netted with left-footed finishes before half-time to ease the loss of seven-goal striker August Priske with a knee problem.

It put City on their way to their sixth win in eight and extended their unbeaten Championship home start to seven games.

Cochrane netted when he lashed home a loose ball from 30 yards when Millwall failed to clear a long pass and Phil Neumann's shot hit a defender. Goalkeeper Max Crocombe was motionless on his line as Cochrane netted for the second successive game.

Millwall forced City goalkeeper Ryan Allsop into a flying save from Caleb Taylor's glancing header following a long throw and Kyrell Lisbie hooked over from the rebound.

City made the visitors pay by doubling their lead in the 16th minute. Bird steered home a left-footed drive from 15 yards after sidestepping Derek Mazou-Sacko before taking on Taylor to celebrate his first start for Birmingham.

Blues continued to threaten and Stansfield's curling shot was palmed away by Crocombe before Jhon Solis' downward header bounced straight at the Millwall goalkeeper.

But in between Millwall wasted the opportunity to reduce the arrears when former City striker Lyndon Dykes flashed a rising drive over the bar as he fell. Jake Cooper then scooped a similar effort over from Lisbie's low cross.

Blues made them pay by making it 3-0 with a fine breakaway goal in the 29th minute. Stansfield took Bird's pass and ran at the defence before cutting inside Cooper and sending a left-footed drive through Taylor's legs into the bottom corner from just outside the box.

The home side continued to hold the upper hand following the restart, although it was Millwall who showed first. Cooper fired straight at Allsop but Crocombe remained the busier of the two keepers.

Crocombe had to dive to his right to keep out Stansfield's shot on the turn from the edge of the box and then he smothered another Stansfield effort and Patrick Roberts's curling shot.

Millwall's closest effort was a thunderous shot from Camiel Neghli that shook the crossbar in the 75th minute.

Substitute Carlos Vicente went within a whisker of making it 4-0 when his angled shot came off the inside of a post and rolled back to Crocombe.

"We are in a position we deserve to be in. Sometimes you go into a false position and we snuck in.

"But we have earned it with our performances and the way the team looks. We've got to enjoy it and take belief and confidence from it. We have made good strides so far.

"It was a big win against a very good opponent. We made a perfect start scoring inside the first minute.

"I wanted us to continue with the same fight, organisation and physicality and with the ball try to be as fluid as we could and there was a lot to like in the first half."

"We conceded in the first minute, then we had an opportunity to equalise but Kyrell Lisbie put it over the bar. We went gung-ho looking for an equaliser and got hit by a sucker punch.

"They broke up the pitch and scored from outside the box and then we got another opportunity to score and didn't take it. They then broke again and scored the third goal. The game was done at 3-0.

"I thought it wasn't just a case of 'we missed, they scored' but after the first goal, we lacked discipline in the middle of the pitch. The space in front of the two centre-backs was too vacant.

"We needed to be more clinical in the final third, stop the transition and, in two-versus-one situations, make the extra man count."

articles.title: Queens Park Rangers 1-1 Burnley: Jonathan Varane earns a point for QPR
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Queens Park Rangers and Burnley at the MATRADE Loftus Road Stadium on Tuesday night; Jonathan Varane earns point for QPR
articles.body:
Largie Ramazani had Burnley dreaming of only their second victory of the season when he fired them ahead at Loftus Road.

But Varane's second-half strike earned Rangers a point, with a little help from Burnley goalkeeper Gregoire Coudert.

The Clarets arrived in west London with one win in 13 Championship games and already on a second manager of the season after Nicky Hayen was sacked last week.

QPR came into the match after a topsy turvy October, hammering Derby 4-1 and Swansea 5-0 at home, while losing 3-0 at Birmingham and, on Saturday, 4-1 at Southampton.

The hosts almost got off to the perfect start after Harvey Vale won a free-kick on the edge of the box, but the midfielder curled his effort inches wide.

Rangers wideman Paul Smyth then cut inside Hjalmar Ekdal only to pull his shot just wide of the near post, before captain Jimmy Dunne's long-range drive cleared the crossbar.

But out of nothing, Burnley took the lead with seven minutes of a one-sided first half remaining.

Coudert's clearance was met with a poor header from Rangers defender Ronnie Edwards.

Jamie Vardy cleverly worked the second ball out to Leeds loanee Ramazani, who struck a sweet 20-yard drive past Pierce Charles, the Rangers goalkeeper getting a hand to the ball but not keeping it out.

Moments later Vardy thought he had set up a second for Andreas Hountondji, who tucked the ball past Charles only to be flagged offside.

Rangers almost hit back before half-time through Edwards' deflected shot, but Coudert got down to make a fine save.

They should have equalised just after the break when Vale whipped in a free-kick but Dunne uncharacteristically missed a free header.

Rangers boss Julien Stephan made a double change on the hour and the subs almost combined to equalise with their first touches, Rayan Kolli pulling the ball back for Ilias Chair, who blazed over the crossbar.

However, the hosts hauled themselves level in the 65th minute when Chair teed up Varane, whose shot from the edge of the box slipped under Coudert's glove and into the net.

Vardy could have won it for the Clarets - and probably would have done 10 years ago - when he was put through by Hountondji late on.

The 39-year-old former Premier League winner let the ball run across him, but then buried his angled finish into the side-netting.

"I'm frustrated with the result. I enjoyed the performance.

"We should have scored one or two in the first 20 minutes. Then they scored with their first shot and we missed some easy passes.

"In the second half I thought we had the chances not only to equalise but to win. We were really dominant but it's a lack of efficiency which is the difference between us and the teams at the top."

"We were very close to taking three points but when you see the game, one point is good. The team is together and trying to win games.

"We missed a bit of quality. With the ball I think we can do better. But one point, Saturday, one point today, hopefully next we can get three. But at the moment I'm happy with what I see."

articles.title: Preston 2-3 Sheffield United: Sydie Peck's hat-trick sees Blades to victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Preston North End and Sheffield United at Deepdale on Tuesday night; Sydie Peck scores a first career hat-trick in Blades victory.
articles.body:
The 22-year-old inadvertently equalised with an intended cross in the 27th minute, put his team ahead with a gorgeous second from just outside the box 10 minutes later, and sealed his treble with a tap-in on the stroke of the interval.

Leo Leroy had put the hosts in front after just two minutes with a clinical finish and substitute Callum Lang set up a grandstand finish with a composed 77th-minute consolation.

It is the first time Sheffield United have managed back-to-back wins this season but that makes it just one point out of 18 for new Preston manager Graham Alexander.

North End had made a fantastic start as Andrew Hughes stole the ball off a sleeping Tahith Chong before laying it off to Andrija Vukcevic, whose cutback was scuffed by Andrew Moran but then emphatically slammed home from the centre of the box by Leroy.

Chong nearly atoned for his error inside 10 minutes with a purposeful run and wicked delivery that Ben Brereton Diaz thumped just over the bar on the turn from a similar position to where the goal had been scored.

Preston's strong start was marred by the loss of Johnny Kenny, who left the pitch clutching his hamstring for Lang after just 13 minutes, and the nature of the equaliser was a bitter pill to taste as Peck's teasing cross evaded everyone and sneaked into the far corner.

There was nothing inadvertent about Peck's 37th-minute second, however, as he nicked the ball away from a stranded Daniel Iversen, chasing Brereton Diaz's ball forward before showing remarkable composure to find the top corner from 20 yards, firing past the despairing Preston keeper and six white and blue shirts that had tried to recover.

In first-half stoppage time, two became three for the homegrown talent and it was a poacher's finish to prod Romelle Donovan's driven cross over the line from point-blank range to put the Blades in control.

Liam Lindsay came on as part of a double change Alexander made at the interval and the 31-year-old was left for dead within minutes as Chong stormed inside from the right before curling just wide, and his rude awakening continued in the 51st minute as Peck nearly placed Hamza Choudhury's tee-up into the net for his fourth, but Iversen parried to safety.

As the game looked like fizzling out for the Lilywhites, two of the substitutes combined when Alfie Devine, who came on for Jusef Erabi just after the hour, rolled the ball across a day-dreaming Blades defence and Lang slotted a first-time effort into the corner, but a comeback never materialised.

"There are times when we might look like we don't care or we're not fully committed but we are. We're just human beings and if you have that period for a long time, six to eight months or something (of struggling) and it can wear you down a bit but it's only us who can get ourselves out of it.

"We have to find a way of creating that mentality, that anger, because that's what I thought we saw in the second half. There was an anger about our team. A controlled anger.

"We conceded a goal and then, I don't think it's an intentional drop of effort, I think it's just a human-nature thing in that we maybe feel a bit sorry for ourselves a little bit and maybe lose a bit of confidence."

"His all-round performance was excellent. (We) were talking about playing him higher, putting him in the box and making forward runs. He's done it right throughout his young career - scored goals - and he needs to score more.

"I spoke to him about Leicester last season, where he got a couple, and he's got that in his locker. He's a touch disappointed because he's had a couple more opportunities in the second half. We got into some great positions.

"(Tahith) Chong should score, Sydie possibly should score, I'm not going to be greedy and say every opportunity we have we should score from but we created enough to take the game away from the opposition. Sydie will get the headlines and rightly so."

articles.title: Derby 0-4 Norwich: More pressure on John Eustace after rampant Canaries win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Derby County and Norwich City at Pride Park on Tuesday night; Canaries pile more pressure on struggling Rams and their boss John Eustace.
articles.body:
On his 47th birthday, Eustace saw his side ripped apart by the pace and movement of the Canaries, who scored three times before the break.

Anthony Musaba, Paris Maghoma and Darlin Yongwa put Norwich in complete control before substitute Jovon Makama wrapped up a third straight win for the visitors and condemned Derby to a fourth defeat in five games.

Derby have won only once this season and Friday night's home game with Bolton now looks like a huge one for Eustace.

They went into the game as only one of two teams without a home win in the Championship and they fell behind in the eighth minute. Jack Stacey crossed from the right and although Yongwa's header was saved, Musaba slammed the rebound into the roof of the net.

Musaba had a great chance to score his second in the 15th minute when Andre Brooks played him in but his low shot struck the legs of goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterstrom.

Norwich looked like scoring every time they came forward and after Zetterstrom made a reflex save to deny Mathias Kvistgaarden, Maghoma made it two with a curling effort from the edge of the box in the 27th minute.

Boos rang out from the home fans and only the woodwork denied Norwich a third when Stacey's shot hit the inside of a post and was cleared off the line by Alex Mowatt.

It got even worse for Derby just before half-time when they were torn apart again and after Brooks fired the ball in from the right, Yongwa made no mistake from 12 yards.

The half-time whistle was met with another chorus of disapproval from the home fans and it was no surprise when Derby made three substitutions for the second half.

Derby at least had an effort on target with a Carlton Morris header forcing Daniel Grimshaw into a diving save and there was certainly more urgency about their play but Norwich were not finished.

Makama came to the party in the 66th minute with a rasping drive from the edge of the area which Zetterstrom could not keep out.

That was the signal for Derby fans to head for the exits and some of those who stayed joined in when Norwich fans taunted Eustace with chants of "sacked in the morning".

It was certainly a miserable night for Eustace and Derby, who even at this early stage look like a team fighting relegation.

"To be in the situation we are now is really disappointing.

"There are reasons why, we've got nine defenders out which certainly doesn't help, but collectively we haven't been good enough and I take responsibility for the performances.

"Ultimately you can make as many excuses as you want with injuries and suspensions but I get judged on results and results haven't been good enough.

"The club is much bigger than me and all the great work we've done over the last 16 months has been something I'm very proud of and not to continue that throughout the summer and up to now has been tough.

"Football is about results and to lose 4-0 at home after losing 4-1 at the weekend is not acceptable and it's my head at the table.

"Of course it hurts, I'm a very proud person but the Championship is relentless, it's ruthless and we have a lot of injuries and we have to respect that fact as well.

"It is very frustrating at the moment but I'm not a quitter and I know we can get more out of the group which is something we will keep trying to do."

"I'm really pleased with what the team did, we could have scored more than the four goals and keeping a clean sheet after a long time will also help the team with their confidence.

"The structure of the team is good and I've seen a lot of positives with the guys who started and the guys who came on. That's what I want to see, no complacency and a mature game in controlling it in most of the moments.

"The group knows me for a long time and I've said the message a lot of times, I hate it when people become complacent, I want to see a hungry team full of desire for more and not to be happy with where they are."

articles.title: Blackburn 1-2 Stoke City: Jack McGlynn steers Potters to victory
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Blackburn Rovers and Stoke City at Ewood Park on Tuesday night; Jack McGlynn stars again as Stoke claim another crucial win.
articles.body:
After weathering early Blackburn pressure, McGlynn caught everyone off guard in the 43rd minute, finding the net with a spectacular set piece from the left instead of the expected cross to notch his fourth of the campaign.

Substitute Moussa Baradji's own goal in the 68th minute gave the Potters a deserved cushion as they seemed set for a comfortable victory.

But Andri Gudjohnsen's tap-in halved the deficit in the 87th minute and the Icelandic forward thought he had equalised three minutes later when skilfully steering a header into the far corner but referee Andrew Kitchen penalised the striker for a push, much to the fury of the Rovers fans and coaching staff.

Despite the late scare, Stoke held on to make it eight wins in 11 and move level on goal difference with second-placed Birmingham.

Stoke's victory here last season owed much to Viktor Johansson's heroics and he was at it again within four minutes when he produced a stunning stop to tip Todd Cantwell's rasping 18-yard drive behind.

Johansson was needed again close to the half hour when Hayden Carter pounced on a loose ball and strode forward into the space to unleash a low drive that the Swede pushed wide for a corner.

Despite their dominance, Rovers fell behind just before the break thanks to an outrageous free-kick from McGlynn. Wide on the left, the American went for goal rather than sending in a cross everyone was expecting and while Balazs Toth got a hand to it, the referee checked his watch to indicate it was over the line.

Dapo Afolayan planted a header wide of the far post after meeting Jayden Fevrier's right-wing cross, as Rovers tried to respond.

Robert Bozenik spurned a glorious chance just after the hour when played through by Million Manhoef, but he could not slot beyond the outstretched Toth.

Stoke recycled possession, the ball fell to Ben Johnson on the edge of the area and his venomous strike deflected wide with Toth well beaten.

The visitors' pressure finally told in the 68th minute when Manhoef was given time and space to race through Blackburn's defence and though Toth pulled off a sharp save down to his left, substitute Yuri Ribeiro's attempted clearance hit fellow replacement Baradji and rebounded into the empty net.

Gudjohnsen handed Rovers a lifeline three minutes from time when Johansson failed to hold Sam Morsy's shot, pouncing for his ninth of the season and he thought he had helped Rovers to a great escape with a towering header three minutes later from Gady Beyuku's cross but it was controversially ruled out and Stoke held on.

"Having watched it back, it's embarrassing really. People come to watch football to see entertainment and goals.

"Listen, I can't understand it really. I've watched it back. Does he put his hands up? Yes because the guy is going to back into him, to protect himself and hold him off. Is it a forward motion and a push? No. Does the guy throw his arms up in the air? Yes. I think the referee gets it hugely wrong. Hugely wrong.

"What hurts a little bit more is the inconsistency of the officials, I suppose.

"Thinking back a few weeks to West Brom away when Gudjohnsen gets blatantly pushed with two hands. Play on, they go down the other end, get a penalty, get back to two each and then win the game late on. Just the inconsistency of it.

"I thought ultimately we played pretty well tonight. We've played probably not as well and won football matches. There you go, that's the game."

"You look for quality in the game and the first goal was that. Honestly, I saw the goalkeeper, where he was stood and I'm thinking 'go on, please see it'.

"He (McGlynn) moved to his right a little bit more to open his stance up and I thought 'go on', and he did it and honestly, he's the only one who could do it out of our team on the pitch. I think (Todd) Cantwell may try that. He's got the audacity to do that, and the ability to do that. I also think there's a couple of others on our team who could do that, who are that good.

"But for Jack, that's incredible. To see it, to spot it, to try it - but to execute it is absolutely fantastic.

"We manage to hold on after the goal was disallowed but rightly so, picked the three points up. Support was absolutely brilliant."

articles.title: West Brom 1-1 Southampton: Samuel Edozie earns point for Saints
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between West Bromwich Albion and Southampton at The Hawthorns on Tuesday night; Isaac Price nets penalty before Samuel Edozie hits back for Saints.
articles.body:
Both teams started the season in promising fashion and taking a point apiece means the sides continue their respective unbeaten runs after a game of two halves.

West Brom completely dominated the first half as Southampton failed to register a single shot in the opening 45 and Isaac Price notched from the penalty spot to give the hosts a deserved half-time lead for his fifth goal of the season.

For all the hosts' dominance, Tonda Eckert's side turned the tables in the second period and found an equaliser through Edozie.

Both teams missed chances to take three points in an entertaining affair which would have lifted either into the top two.

The hosts were fresh off their victory at West Ham, and their confidence showed - they should have been a goal to the good in the fifth minute but Jimmy-Jay Morgan blazed over while one-on-one with Daniel Peretz.

The Baggies continued their sustained period of attack and forced Peretz into a first save when he needed to touch Molumby's effort from range over the crossbar.

West Brom had a chance to get a deserved opener from the spot after Rabby Nzingoula latched onto Molumby's perfectly weighted ball and was brought down by Jack Stephens' lazy leg inside the box.

And Price made no mistake in sending Peretz the wrong way and dispatching right to put West Brom a goal up.

The visitors were unable to deal with West Brom's press and were getting completely ran over by the hosts, and Price should have had his second three minutes before the break but curled wide.

Things could only get better for the Saints after the break, and they certainly started a lot better and were rewarded with a goal with their first shot on target.

Ryan Manning flinged a cross to the far post and Kuryu Matsuki's header across goal landed at the feet of Edozie who smashed in from close range.

West Brom almost reacted perfectly with an equaliser. Callum Styles was first to get his head onto Nat Phillips' cross but his header was cleared off the line by Stephens.

Southampton went searching for a second and could have had one when Finn Azaz tamely aimed at Max O'Leary instead of squaring to Divin Mubama.

It was wave after wave of Saints attack, and West Brom needed O'Leary again to to stop Azaz's deflected cross from going in.

Southampton missed a glorious chance for the win when Azaz put Lewis Dobbin one on one but the substitute was denied by O'Leary when he ought to have scored.

West Brom could have nicked it themselves after Ousmane Diakite carried it 50 yards with a rapid counter-attack, he fed to Tammer Bany who rattled a post.

"Two very good teams. Thought we were really good first half. My only critic really is could we have scored one more and give us a bit more of a cushion.

"The energy we put into it, it was going to be hard to replicate that second half. With them being such a good team, the reaction came and we just couldn't see it out.

"Both teams had chances and it was a good advertisement for the Championship. On a whole, it's a very good performance.

"You expect that (a reaction), because we were so dominant. To limit Southampton to no shots on our goal. We just couldn't get through that 10 minutes where they had it."

"Two very different halves. Take the first half, it's a quick turnaround and I think we've given them too much respect in the first half.

"Second half was a completely different game, there's a couple of chances in there to win it in the second half. If you look at the 90 minutes today I think you take the point. I think it is a fair result, we take it and move on to Preston.

"Two teams that played to win. We had chances to score a second one but fair play to West Brom, they are a good team and not easy to come up against.

"We need to make sure we get three (points) on Saturday, then I think we have played a decent first block."

articles.title: Charlton 0-1 Bolton: Sam Dalby scores Trotters winner as poor run goes on for Addicks
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Charlton Athletic and Bolton Wanderers at The Valley on Tuesday night; Sam Dalby scores the Trotters winner as Addicks misery continues.
articles.body:
The result piles more pressure on Addicks boss Nathan Jones with the south-east Londoners now winless in 11 matches, and a fourth straight Championship loss dropped them to 21st in the table.

Bolton captain Josh Sheehan pulled the midfield strings during the opening 45 minutes and produced a whipped shot wide after five minutes.

Charlton had the first of the minimal openings in the first half on seven minutes. Tyreece Campbell's deep cross picked out Danny McNamara's run to the far post but the right-sided wing-back's attempt to convert was frustrated by Wanderers goalkeeper Jack Bonham.

Charlie Kelman had the ball in the net for the hosts soon after but it was flagged offside.

Bolton went ahead in the 18th minute. Nathaniel Chalobah's misplaced pass gifted Dalby a run on goal and the striker confidently finished past Will Mannion.

Charlton were unable to force Bonham into a save during the first period, aside from a comfortable claim from a tame Kelman attempt early on. Harvey Knibbs headed harmlessly wide from Karlan Grant's cross.

It needed Charlton skipper Lloyd Jones to make a vital block on Max Conway's shot after McNamara lost possession inside the penalty box.

The home support booed their team off at half-time, voicing their frustrations as the Addicks, clearly lacking in confidence, moved the ball too slowly.

Bolton midfielder Atsuki Ito smashed a first time volley wide of the right upright early in the second half.

Kelman produced a first-time header from a decent left wing delivery by Campbell on the hour mark. It proved to be the forward's last action as he was replaced by veteran Matty Godden.

Bonham was penalised for picking up Sheehan's backpass but Wanderers were out quickly to block Knibbs' shot from eight yards out from Grant's short free-kick.

Charlton exerted pressure as the contest wore on but Bolton defended resiliently, typified by a strong display from Akin Famewo, who was also close at the other end of the pitch to connecting with Gaizka Larrazabal's free-kick.

Wanderers substitute Thierry Gale twice had opportunities to finish the contest off but could not beat Mannion.

Campbell sent a 20-yard curler wide at the other end as Bolton picked up a third win in a four-match unbeaten sequence on the road.

"In terms of endeavour, work-rate and passing the football I have zero problem. We have had so many opportunities around the edge of the box.

"We had no problem all night and then we gifted them a goal. They haven't had to work for it in any way. We then did not demonstrate enough attacking quality in the final third.

"We've probably made more positive substitutions tonight than is humanly possible - I got as many attacking players on the pitch. We aren't doing the out-of-possession stuff well enough either and that is a tough recipe.

"All we can do is more work, big them up, give them a cuddle - we do it. We ask them to hit areas and be confident. We work on the final third and know how we can get in behind them and we just don't do it when we cross the white line.

"We have won games here with a lot less possession and a lot less opportunities in the final third."

"It's a huge result for us. It is never easy to get three points away from home on a Tuesday night fixture, especially after a setback for us on Saturday.

"We deserved to win that game and let it slip. It was important we tried to respond and we did that tonight.

"We knew it would be a difficult game with everything going on here. They are not in a great run of form, so we expected them to throw everything at us and we dealt with that really well, especially in the first half when we were nice and calm."

"We've had about seven one-v-ones this season and that's the first one we've been able to take. So there was a bit of doubt - until he hit the net. He took it well. It was a mistake and we managed to pounce on it.

"It gave the players some belief and confidence that we could go and get a result here."

articles.title: Huddersfield 1-1 Luton
articles.summary: League One's two most in-form sides shared the spoils as Huddersfield and Luton drew 1-1 at Accu Stadium.
articles.body:
Leaders Huddersfield controlled much of the first half, and Cameron Humphreys twice went close to scoring direct from inswinging corners: the first hit the bar, the next tipped over by James Shea.

But it was Luton who took the lead on 40 minutes as Huddersfield failed to deal with a long pass up the right to Jamie Donley, with Jordan Clark ultimately finishing to the bottom corner off Kasey Palmer's knockdown.

Huddersfield came out at a higher tempo after the break, and within four minutes of the restart they had their equaliser, Derensili Sanches Fernandes crossing for Joe Taylor to volley home his tenth goal of the season against his former club.

The game became attritional as both teams tired, however, and both sides had to settle for a point.

That extends the Terriers' lead over Stockport to three points, while Luton move up to third place and just two points shy of second.

articles.title: Barcelona 3-0 Aston Villa: Raphinha double sees Barca go second in Champions League standings
articles.summary: Match report as Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0 in the Champions League; Raphinha's second-half double, after Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring early on, saw the hosts to a comfortable victory; Barca move above Villa into second in the league standings
articles.body:
Villa boss Emery returned to his homeland on his 55th birthday and with his team in great form having lost just one of their previous nine encounters, only to come crashing down in the driving Catalan rain.

The home side have been in free-scoring form this season, averaging four goals a game and they got on the scoresheet within seven minutes. Joao Gomes laid the ball on a plate to, of all people, Lamine Yamal, for the Spain forward's 13th goal of this campaign. He also has 11 assists to his name.

Raphinha made Villa's first game at the Nou Camp for 46 years a miserable one with a quickfire double at the start of the second half to end any hopes the visitors had of getting back into the contest as Hansi Flick's side moved above their opponents into second in the table.

7: GOAL! Suzuki goes short from the goal kick and the midfielder Joao Gomes plays a blind pass across his own penalty area, which falls straight to Lamine Yamal, who curls his shot into the far corner with ease.

19: CHANCE! Jackson breaks down the right and finds Manzambi, but he mishits the sweeping shot and it goes wide!

20: HUGE CHANCE! Jackson times his run perfectly and is played through by Manzambi, but Garcia pokes it clear after meeting the striker outside the penalty area.

26: CHANCE! Suzuki plays a dangerous pass to Joao Gomes and Barcelona pounce. The Villa goalkeeper is able to beat Gordon's shot though.

52: GOAL! Raphinha fires a shot on goal from just inside the area and a big deflection sends it trickling into the back of the net after wrong-footing Suzuki.

64: GOAL! Cancelo drives down the left but plays the cross with the outside of the boot into the box. It bends around the defence, perfectly into Raphinha's path, before it's tapped home with ease.

69: POST! Goretzka meets the corner and glances the header towards goal but it grazes the post! Jackson was there but didn't gamble to tap it in.

Merson: Villa will be rueing missed first-half chances

Sky Sports' Paul Merson on Soccer Special:

"There was not a lot [of difference between the sides] in the first half; they [Villa] shot themselves in the foot early doors. After that, they had good chances to score and should have scored at least one of them.

"Come out second half and Barcelona were different class, by far the better team. Villa really never looked like getting back into it second half.

"So a solid performance, but they'll be rueing their chances in the first half. Villa, second half, never in the game. It was a bit of a free swing tonight. And as I said, in the first half they've done well, second half not good enough."

"The result is not good. A lot of things were positive but it was not enough to get the result.

"How we are building the team is clear in 90 minutes. We have young players, talented players and past players but we must try and get our structure.

"We made mistakes but we overcame these mistakes. Today, more or less, after the mistake we made, we were creating chances and facing them.

"With the chances we had in the first half, maybe it would be different, but we were not clinical. We had chances to score and did not score.

"We have nine points because we did good work. We should be realistic but, at the same time, feel good.

"We need experiences for the players. Today was very important. To use it to get better.

"Good experience, bad result. At this level, you must be ruthless and avoid mistakes."

The numbers from Villa's loss in Barcelona

Aston Villa suffered their joint-heaviest defeat in major European competition, having also lost by three goals to Royal Antwerp in September 1975 (1-4) and Internazionale in November 1990 (0-3), both in the UEFA Cup.

No Premier League side has committed more errors leading to goals in all competitions this season than Aston Villa (7, level with Sunderland).

John McGinn made his 38th appearance for Aston Villa in major European competition - the outright most for the club.

articles.title: El Unicaja somete al combativo Pallacanestro Reggiana con récord de triples
articles.standfirst: Amine Noua (27+5), Kendrick Perry (17+3+9) y Matt Thomas (20+3+2) comandan el sufrido triunfo de los malagueños (99-94), que anotaron 19 triples
articles.summary: Amine Noua (27+5), Kendrick Perry (17+3+9) y Matt Thomas (20+3+2) comandan el sufrido triunfo de los malagueños (99-94), que anotaron 19 triples
articles.body: El Unicaja consiguió una importante victoria ante el Pallacanestro Reggiana (99-94) en un encuentro marcado por el acierto de ambos equipos desde el perímetro. Los malagueños encontraron en el triple su principal arma, especialmente en un espectacular tercer cuarto en el que anotaron ocho lanzamientos exteriores. Pese a llegar a disfrutar de una renta de 18 puntos, los italianos apretaron en los últimos minutos y obligaron a los de Txus Vidorreta a no bajar la guardia. Amine Noua, con 27 puntos, cinco rebotes y 27 de valoración, fue el jugador más destacado. Además, los 19 triples anotados establecieron un nuevo récord del club en la BCL. El encuentro arrancó con un Unicaja acertado, liderado por Brazdeikis y Noua (7-4). Sin embargo, el Reggiana reaccionó rápidamente con tres triples consecutivos y un 2+1 de Thor que le permitió tomar el mando (10-16). Matt Thomas y Barreiro intentaron responder desde el perímetro, pero Visconti mantuvo a los italianos por delante al término del primer cuarto (16-25). La dinámica continuó en el segundo periodo. Dos triples de Kalinoski permitieron al Unicaja acercarse hasta los dos puntos (31-33), aunque el conjunto visitante volvió a encontrar soluciones ofensivas para conservar su ventaja. Perry y Thomas lideraron la reacción local con dos parciales de 5-0 que permitieron a los malagueños recuperar momentáneamente el control. Sin embargo, una penetración de Uglietti dejó las tablas en el marcador al descanso (43-43). Tras la reanudación, el Reggiana volvió a adelantarse gracias a su acierto exterior (45-50), pero la respuesta cajista fue contundente. Kalinoski y Perry igualaron el choque antes de que Noua y Thomas comenzaran a marcar diferencias desde el triple. El Unicaja encontró su mejor versión ofensiva y encadenó ocho lanzamientos exteriores en el periodo, con Perry, Thomas y Noua como protagonistas. La ventaja llegó a alcanzar los once puntos al cierre del tercer cuarto (75-64). El festival anotador dejó varios registros históricos. Los 19 triples convertidos suponen la mejor marca del Unicaja en un partido de la BCL. Además, Matt Thomas (6) y Noua (5) alcanzaron al menos cinco aciertos desde el perímetro, igualando un registro que el club había conseguido otras cuatro veces. También cuatro jugadores anotaron tres o más triples: Thomas, Noua, Kalinoski (3) y Perry (3). En el último cuarto, el Unicaja llegó a disfrutar de una máxima ventaja de 18 puntos (98-80), con Noua nuevamente como referencia ofensiva. Sin embargo, el Reggiana no se rindió. Los triples de Severini y Barford reactivaron a los italianos, que aprovecharon el desacierto malagueño para acercarse peligrosamente hasta el 98-94. Vidorreta tuvo que detener el encuentro, aunque la reacción visitante no terminó ahí. 99 - Unicaja (16+27+32+24): Perry (17), Kalinoski (9), Brazdeikis (7), Noua (27), Kravish (8) -quinteto inicial- Barreiro (3), Lukosius (6), Djedovic (-), Pantzar (2), Thomas (20), Hernangómez (-). 94 - Pallacanestro Reggiana (25+18+21+30): Edwards (2), Uglietti (7), Woldetensae (9), Echenique (12), Thor (14) -quinteto inicial- Barford (22), Visconti (15), Manfredotti (-), Severini (11), Ogbeide (2). articles.title: El Manchester United 'aCunha' una remontada salvadora
articles.standfirst: Los 'Red Devils' no ganaban desde el 10 de septiembre... y Carrick evita el despido
articles.summary: Los 'Red Devils' no ganaban desde el 10 de septiembre... y Carrick evita el despido
articles.body: Del drama... al éxtasis. El Manchester United levantó un 0-2 en contra para sumar su primera victoria desde el 10 de septiembre. Michael Carrick salva el puesto gracias a un Matheus Cunha que firmó doblete y provocó un penalti... antes de ser expulsado. La Roma, como ante el Real Madrid en Italia, sufrió una dramática remontada en contra. El partido tuvo dos partes muy diferenciadas. De primeras, ni tener que jugar con su tercero portero (Devis Vásquez, que debutaba en Champions) frenó a una Roma que se divirtió en Mánchester durante 45 minutos. A los 18' de arrancar, el equipo de Gasperini ya ganaba 0-2 en Old Trafford. Nadie nunca había anotado dos tantos tan rápido como visitante en competición europea en la casa del Manchester United. Otro récord negativo en una 'era mancuniana' con más disgustos que alegrías. Primero Soulé, tras un gran pase de Rodrigo Mora, después Malen, de penalti. Era un recital italiano. El colapso del equipo de Carrick era total. Y aunque la grada 'perdonaba' al ex centrocampista, la tomaba con los jugadores. El partido se llegó a parar unos instantes por lanzamiento de pelotas de goma desde uno de los fondos del que antaño fuera el 'Teatro de los Sueños'. Pasaban los minutos y, de hecho, el 0-3 estaba más cerca que el intento de remontada. Antes del descanso, Lammens sacó una gran mano ante Malen y Soulé rozó la escuadra con un disparo precioso. El fútbol, sin embargo, es cuestión de estados de ánimo y el Manchester United, que había estado al borde del abismo, volvió al partido. Y todo, pese a la lesión de Baleba. Del drama... a una ilusión que creció con el paso de los minutos. Gil Manzano señaló un discutible penalti sobre Cunha que Bruno Fernandes, en primera instancia, falló. Todo muy Manchester United. Pero hubo invasión de campo de los italianos, en la parte contraria del área a la del rechace, y la parada de Vásquez quedó en nada. El luso anotó a la segunda. Fueron los mejores minutos del equipo de Carrick. El United, renacido, se topó con el palo por partida doble en un mano a mano de Mbeumo. La Roma, con los fantasmas del Olímpico y el Real Madrid en la cabeza, no lo cerró... y llegó el empate. Un fallo grave de Balerdi y tanto de Cunha. El frenesí se mantuvo y fue el ex Atlético el que se consagró como héroe absoluto de una noche para el recuerdo. Tras un gran contol, hizo el 3-2 para darle la vuelta al partido. Como ante el Real Madrid, a la Roma se le fue una ventaja de dos goles. del 3-1 al 3-4 en el Olímpico, del 0-2 al 3-2 hoy... en Old Trafford. El United y Carrick, mientras, asoman la cabeza tras una crisis de casi dos meses.

articles.title: Cómodo triunfo del Asisa Joventut en cancha del Porto
articles.standfirst: Nico Laprovittola (23 con 6/9 triples) y Álex Reyes (12+3+2) lideran la victoria de los verdinegros (64-81), que siguen invictos en la BCL
articles.summary: Nico Laprovittola (23 con 6/9 triples) y Álex Reyes (12+3+2) lideran la victoria de los verdinegros (64-81), que siguen invictos en la BCL
articles.body: El Asisa Joventut logró este martes su primer triunfo a domicilio de la temporada, en Portugal, al derrotar al Oporto por 64-81 en un duelo dominado mayormente por los de Dani Miret. Un parcial de 6-26 en el segundo cuarto fue clave para que los catalanes sumaran el tercer triunfo en la Liga de Campeones para seguir líderes invictos del grupo H. Pese al dominio de la Penya, fue el Oporto el equipo que mejor comenzó el encuentro, con un acertado Childe Dundao, que puso el 10-9 en los primeros cinco minutos de partido. En los minutos posteriores no hubo apenas canastas, con los dos equipos muy imprecisos en sus respectivos aros, y se llegó al final del primer cuarto con un ajustado 17-14. En el segundo periodo cambió totalmente el guion del partido, con un Asisa Joventut que vio cómo Nico Laprovittola lideró al equipo para lograr la primera ventaja del partido (19-26, min. 14). Los portugueses no reaccionaron, y la Penya lo aprovechó con una lluvia de triples comandada por Álex Reyes para poner la máxima del partido para los suyos (19-35, min. 17). El acierto en los verdinegros se mantuvo, y se llegó al descanso con un 23-40 favorable para los de Dani Miret, aunque el choque no estaba ni mucho menos sentenciado. En la reanudación se volvió a ver la mejor versión del Oporto y unos buenos minutos de Thomas Bropleh pusieron a su equipo con una desventaja de tan sólo 11 puntos (33-44, min. 24). Durante los seis minutos restantes de tercer cuarto hubo muy poca anotación y el Asisa Joventut logró cerrarlo con un 39-51 a favor tras diversas acciones positivas del recién llegado Nikola Radicevic. Ya en el último cuarto, el Asisa Joventut volvió a depender de Laprovittola para coger una buena renta y poner tierra de por medio en el Palacio de Congresos de Matosinhos (44-58, min. 33). El base argentino siguió con su festival particular y otro triple suyo dejó el partido prácticamente visto para sentencia a falta de cuatro minutos para el final (49-66, min. 36). Al final, el Asisa Joventut venció a domicilio al Oporto por 64-81 para sumar la tercera victoria en la Liga de Campeones de la FIBA. 64. articles.title: Raphinha, Lamal fire Barcelona to 3-0 Champions League win over Aston Villa
articles.summary: Barca took early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued fine goal-scoring form with a second-half brace.
articles.body:
Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the football competition.

Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goal-scoring form with a second-half brace.

Barca bounced back after defeat to champions Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top-eight league phase berth.

Manager Unai Emery’s Villa competed well in the first half, but were eventually undone by Barca’s greater ability in the final third.

The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel , who died of a cardiac arrest on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second-division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world.

“Yes, it was [a good win]; I want to dedicate this win to the fans, but today I don’t want to talk about football, I want to send a message to the family of Jesus – may he rest in peace,” Raphinha told Movistar.

“This can happen to anyone; it’s very tough … you’re going to play a game, and the same thing can happen to you…

“From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family.”

Villa captain John McGinn had only visited Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to.

The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute.

The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high, and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

Emery, who endured one of the worst nights of his career away at Barca when helming PSG in 2017 during a 6-1 defeat, may have feared the worst.

However, Villa reacted strongly, and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes’s effort.

Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball.

Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca’s pressing.

Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end.

Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner.

Cancelo powered a strike narrowly over before setting up Raphinha for Barcelona’s third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot.

The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal of the season across all competitions.

Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games.

Elsewhere on Tuesday, Bayern ‌Munich and PSG underlined their Champions ⁠League title ⁠credentials with victories over Atletico Madrid and Villarreal respectively, while Manchester United came ⁠from two goals down to snatch a dramatic win over AS Roma.

Bayern broke down a stubborn Atletico ⁠side in Madrid as second-half goals from Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer secured victory, while PSG set a record as the fastest team to score four goals in ‌a Champions League match on their way to a 6-0 victory.

At Old Trafford, Matheus Cunha struck twice in quick succession after the break as United overturned a two-goal deficit to beat Roma 3-2, the comeback following protests by home supporters.

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: "Ha sido difícil, ha habido mentiras sobre muchas cosas..."
articles.standfirst: El capitán de los 'Red Devils' habló tras la remontada ante la Roma
articles.summary: El capitán de los 'Red Devils' habló tras la remontada ante la Roma
articles.body: Tras una remontada épica en la que el Manchester United pasó del 0-2 al 3-2 en Old Trafford, Bruno Fernandes dio la cara en rueda de prensa. El capitán del United celebró la primera victoria 'Red Devil' desde el pasado 10 de septiembre. Un triunfo que, desde luego, salva a Carrick... por ahora. "No necesitamos salvar el puesto de nadie. El club necesitaba esa victoria, los jugadores necesitaban esa victoria. Hemos estado trabajando muy duro para salir de esta situación todos juntos. Ha sido difícil, ha habido mucha especulación en los medios. Muchas mentiras sobre muchas cosas que han pasado entre el entrenador y yo, que hemos aclarado, y luego el entrenador tomó la decisión de ponerme en el banquillo porque no estoy rindiendo", analizaba el luso. "Todos pensaron que era un castigo por mis palabras. Si lo fue, fue justo. El entrenador es quien toma las decisiones. Eso no cambia la confianza que tengo en el entrenador, el cuerpo técnico y todos los jugadores de este club. No cambia mi objetivo de ganar todos los partidos que tengo por delante", ampliaba. Al United ahora, no obstante, le vienen pruebas muy duras: recibe al Aston Villa antes del parón... y viaja a Anfield para medirse el Liverpool a la vuelta.

articles.body: Matheus Cunha's three-minute brace flipped Manchester United's fortunes around during a come-from-behind 3-2 win against Roma at Old Trafford on Tuesday.Roma seemed on its way to sending the Red Devils to a 10th straight game without a win after Matìas Soulè and Donyell Malen scored six minutes apart early in the first half. The home crowd booed the players off the pitch after the first 45 minutes, but the second-half finish would alter their moods dramatically.Bruno Fernandes got Manchester United on the board with a 58th-minute penalty. As the match entered the final 10 minutes, Cunha changed the trajectory of it all, thanks to a mistake at the back by Leonardo Balerdi, allowing the Brazilian to equalize.But Cunha wasn't done. articles.title: Lautaro Spatz, jugador del Andorra: "Quienes conocemos a Owono sabemos la clase de persona que es y lo mucho que está sufriendo"
articles.standfirst: El central del conjunto andorrano manda sus condolencias a la familia de Jesús de Miguel
articles.summary: El central del conjunto andorrano manda sus condolencias a la familia de Jesús de Miguel
articles.body: Lautaro Spatz, jugador del Andorra, escribió un largo mensaje en Instagram reflexionando tras la muerte de Jesús de Miguel, un partido en el que él estaba sobre el césped en el momento del golpe de Owono al delantero del Tenerife. Además de mandar sus condolencias a la familia de De Miguel, tiene unas palabras para su compañero Owono y desvela cómo está viviendo estos duros momentos. Hay momentos en los que el fútbol deja de tener sentido. Momentos que te marcan para siempre y que te hacen darte cuenta de lo frágil que puede ser la vida. Lo que vivimos es algo que ninguno de nosotros olvidará jamás. Una tragedia que nos ha dejado completamente rotos, sin palabras y con una tristeza difícil de explicar. En primer lugar, quiero trasladar mi más sincero pésame y todo mi cariño a la familia, amigos y seres queridos de Jesús, así como a toda la afición chicharrera y al mundo del fútbol. Desde ayer, toda la plantilla del FC Andorra estamos conmocionados, hundidos y afectados por lo sucedido. Es una tragedia que jamás hubiéramos imaginado vivir en un terreno de juego. También quiero tener unas palabras para mi compañero, portero y amigo; que está profundamente afectado por lo ocurrido. Quienes lo conocemos sabemos la clase de persona que es, lo mucho que está sufriendo en estos momentos y que jamás tendría intención de hacerle daño a nadie. En el fútbol existen acciones fortuitas, pero nadie puede imaginar que una de ellas pueda terminar con unas consecuencias tan trágicas. Hoy el fútbol no importa. Solo queda acompañar en el dolor, mostrar el máximo respeto y mandar toda nuestra fuerza a la familia y a quienes están sufriendo esta terrible pérdida. Descansa en paz, Demi".

articles.title: What if high school football had a 12-team national playoff? Here's our Super 25 field
articles.summary: The first CFP reveal is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 3. Here's a look at how a hypothetical high school playoff could look like.
articles.body:
The first College Football Playoff Rankings are set to be revealed on Tuesday, Nov. 3.

While college football fans are eager for the first official 12-team bracket preview of what is to come for the actual bracket in December, there is still plenty of games left to be played.

Meanwhile, we are entering the homestretch for high school football. Many states have already entered the postseason , while weeks and weeks of the regular season have given us a clearer picture of which teams are the best in the nation.

Santa Margarita (Rancho Santa Margarita, CA) continues to be the No. 1 team in the USA TODAY Sports Super 25 rankings this week, with St. Thomas Aquinas (Fort Lauderdale, FL) nipping at its heels at No. 2.

While we don't actually have a national playoff for high school football, here's a look at what a bracket for a potential high school playoff would look like, based on the latest Super 25 rankings.

USA TODAY Sports Super 25 rankings playoff bracket

First things first, the top five seeds would go to the top teams in each of the regions in the Super 15 rankings.

articles.title: Bayern teenager Karl becomes fourth youngest to score 5 career goals in Champions League
articles.summary: MADRID (AP) — Bayern Munich's Lennart Karl was on target in a 2-0 victory at Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, becoming the fourth youngest player to score five go...
articles.body:
MADRID (AP) — Bayern Munich's Lennart Karl was on target in a 2-0 victory at Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, becoming the fourth youngest player to score five goals in the Champions League.

Harry Kane promised to lead Bayern through a wave of absences that included head coach Vincent Kompany, and he did so despite failing to score for a second straight game since winning the Ballon d'Or .

The Germany midfielder Karl broke the deadlock in the 54th minute after Robin Le Normand failed to clear the ball following a deflected shot from Tom Bischof.

Karl is aged 18 years and 254 days. Only Lamine Yamal (17 years and 291 days), Kylian Mbappé (18 years and 120 days) and Raúl (18 years and 162 days) were younger when they reached five goals, according to organizer UEFA.

He has also scored in a 4-0 win against Club Brugge, a 3-1 defeat to Arsenal, a 3-1 win over Sporting and a 4-1 victory over Atalanta.

Karl almost scored before his goal in Madrid, when Kane fed him but his attempt just went over the bar.

Kane played a role in the second goal, releasing Konrad Laimer to fire the ball into the roof of the net.

The England forward came close to scoring with a volley in the first half and two attempts in the second.

articles.title: El Bayern saca pecho: "Dominamos por completo desde el primer minuto hasta el 93"
articles.standfirst: Neuer y Laimer, que se llevó el trofeo MVP, destacaron la superioridad de su equipo sobre el Atlético
articles.summary: Neuer y Laimer, que se llevó el trofeo MVP, destacaron la superioridad de su equipo sobre el Atlético
articles.body: El Bayern de Múnich se llevó la victoria con merecimiento en su visita al Atlético. Fueron superiores los alemanes que, además, aprovecharon un error de Le Normand para adelantarse en el marcador ya en la segunda parte. Los teutones terminaron el encuentro con casi un 60% de posesión, por momentos rondaron el 70%, y 19 remates, cinco de ellos a portería. Con este triunfo, suman ocho puntos en la Champions tras los cuatro partidos que han disputado. Tras el encuentro, Neuer y Laimer, que se llevó el trofeo MVP, destacaron la superioridad de su equipo sobre el Atlético. "Diría que dominamos por completo desde el primer minuto hasta el 93. No importaba lo que el Atlético nos planteara, siempre teníamos respuesta", dijo el portero en declaraciones recogidas por el sitio web del Bayern. "Estamos increíblemente contentos, sobre todo teniendo en cuenta las circunstancias, habiendo tenido que dar un paso atrás por las lesiones y lo que ha estado pasando en el Bayern de Múnich últimamente. Pero nos mantuvimos unidos y lo dimos todo para lograr este éxito colectivo hoy. Esto demuestra que somos un equipo y que tenemos respuesta para todo. Creo que algunos dudaban de que pudiéramos competir fuera de casa contra un equipo tan bueno. Responder a eso es sensacional", continuó. De la misma opinión que el portero era Laimer. "Afrontamos el partido sabiendo de lo que éramos capaces. Siempre se habla mucho de ello, pero tenemos mucha confianza en nuestra plantilla. Creo que hoy, durante los 90 minutos, demostramos cómo podemos y queremos jugar al fútbol. Podríamos haber marcado algunos goles más. Es una victoria merecida contra un buen equipo. Estos tres puntos sin duda nos darán un impulso para el próximo partido contra el Mainz y para las próximas semanas", afirmó. Aaron Danks, que ejerció de entrenador del Bayern Múnich, también valoró el rendimiento de sus jugadores: “Estoy muy satisfecho con el rendimiento del equipo. Fue fantástico cómo mantuvimos la portería a cero y cómo creamos ocasiones de gol. Es difícil destacar a un solo jugador, fue, simplemente, un magnífico trabajo en equipo".
